A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TabRep work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original TabRep experiments on seven real datasets, representation ablations, privacy and efficiency evaluations, and synthetic high-cardinality and imbalanced-data experiments.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports training-loss comparisons between TabRep-DDPM and OneHot-DDPM in Figure 6.

M1.justification: The circular CatConverter encoding, DDPM and flow-matching objectives, denoising architecture, and training/sampling algorithms remain unchanged. v5 explains the previously named InvCatConverter operation; this additional documentation does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same seven real datasets and the same high-cardinality and imbalanced synthetic regression scenarios. These synthetic studies already appear in v1 Appendix D.4. The new loss curves reuse existing datasets.

E2.justification: The evaluated baseline and ablation sets are retained, including STaSy, CoDi, TabDDPM, TabSYN, TabDiff, TabFlow and alternative encodings. Figure 6 compares already evaluated encodings. Newly cited TabED and LLM methods are not added to reported experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: v5 adds normalized training loss versus training steps as a diagnostic evaluation in Figure 6, displaying trajectories through 10,000 steps. Existing splits, benchmark metrics, model dimensions and stated training/sampling budgets remain unchanged. Newly specified preprocessing details do not establish revised settings.

E4.justification: Figure 6 adds a focused analysis of whether CatConverter improves convergence and loss stability relative to one-hot encoding across seven datasets. Existing ordering, casting-rate, high-cardinality, imbalance and latent-dimension studies remain; moving the ordering study into Section 5.2 does not make it new.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 20 sampling seeds or iterations using the best-validated model and report means with standard deviations. v5 introduces no new confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run protocol; its loss curves provide no additional uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Matched tabular performance, privacy, timing and appendix results are unchanged. v5 Figure 6 newly reports faster convergence and generally lower normalized loss for TabRep-DDPM versus OneHot-DDPM. Appendix B.3 also newly states limited sensitivity to learning rate, weight decay and batch size, without presenting a supporting sweep.

T1.justification: v5 removes an extra sigma_t^4 denominator from Equation 10, matching v1's appendix derivation, and restricts the statement to minimal n-singular points in Theorem 4.1. Appendix A.1 substantially extends the uniform-prior discussion with an arbitrary categorical-prior derivation, Equations 48–57. However, the new derivation uses unnormalized density-weighted sums as expectations, leaving its claimed generalization unsupported.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same central contribution and headline claims: a dense two-dimensional categorical representation supporting diffusion and flow models, superior synthesis utility, privacy preservation and efficiency. The abstract's claim of exceeding real-data downstream performance is unchanged.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly qualifies lexicographic ordering as a heuristic without semantic optimization and explains how zero-index casting can distort category frequencies, especially under imbalance. It also discusses radius scaling for high cardinality, unexplored unification into a categorical space, and interprets the new loss curves as evidence of improved training stability.

D1.justification: v5 documents atan2-based inverse decoding and nearest-phase projection, specifies adaptive quantile selection as max(min(N/30,1000),10), and identifies the separability classifier as a two-layer MLP. These expand previously incomplete descriptions. Hardware, principal hyperparameters and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 expands related work to cover TabED and energy discrepancy, plus LLM-based tabular generation and augmentation, contrasting their context/token limitations with diffusion scalability. It also cites Chronos for future exploration. These are bounded additions to the retained diffusion-centered positioning.

P1.justification: The overall section sequence and much of the prose remain intact. Changes include targeted explanatory expansions, moving categorical ordering from Appendix B.2 into Section 5.2, adding declarations and limitations, and revising front matter and citation style.

P2.justification: v5 reformats the document throughout for TMLR, changing title and heading typography, running headers, text widths and table layouts. It adds the seven-panel Figure 6, moves v1 Table 7 into the main text as Table 4, rearranges the efficiency displays, and redistributes appendix tables. Existing figures and table contents are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v5 adds useful loss-curve evidence, implementation detail and more specific limitations while retaining the original benchmark evidence. However, its new categorical-prior derivation in Appendix A.1, particularly Equations 52–57, treats unnormalized density-weighted sums as score expectations and variances, so the claimed generalization is not established. The documentation and diagnostic gains coexist with a new theoretical correctness problem, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
